subject: Lophelia reefs
topic: These aren't tropical reefs. They're coral reefs in total darkness.
script:
These aren't tropical reefs. They're coral reefs in total darkness.
Hundreds of meters down off the southeastern United States, cold-water corals build huge mounds.
Unlike shallow corals, they don't need sunlight. They catch food drifting in the current.
Over thousands of years, living and dead coral pile up into hills.
Some of these mounds rise up to three hundred meters tall.
One area off Florida has so many that it's called the Million Mounds.
In twenty nineteen, NOAA explored two healthy reefs here that no one knew existed.
These reefs give food and shelter to fish, crabs and countless other animals.
Did you know coral reefs could grow in the dark?
